# `bin/astra-session`

A tool: run it from the root of an instance (or of the kit, for the kit's own tools).
Source: [`bin/astra-session`](../../../bin/astra-session)

## What it says about itself

```text
Launch Claude Code routed at OpenRouter with OpenAI GPT-6 Astra as the session model.
The external-orchestrator route: a whole session on another provider's model, started by the user.

  bin/astra-session                    interactive session (Astra standard, effort medium)
  bin/astra-session -p "prompt" ...    headless; adds --strict-mcp-config + no-mcp.json
  ASTRA_EFFORT=max bin/astra-session   override the session effort (low|medium|high|xhigh|max)
  ASTRA_MODEL, ASTRA_PRO_MODEL, ASTRA_FABLE_MODEL override the slots below.
Interactive mode needs a terminal on stdin (the user's, never an orchestrator's tool call); headless mode needs
a user approval of exactly this argv (bin/_approval.py check session astra). Each start writes an EXT-SESSION
ledger line. The key is read from $OPENROUTER_KEYFILE (default ~/.config/openrouter/key).

Model slots inside the session:
  opus   -> openai/gpt-6-astra-pro
  fable  -> ~anthropic/claude-fable-latest  (billed through OpenRouter)
  sonnet/haiku -> Claude aliases via OpenRouter: Claude Code's own background calls (auto-mode
                  classifier, titles) use these slots, so they stay on Claude models.
Workers are launched only with bin/run-external, never as subagents (the hook refuses an Agent call of a worker
type): model and effort are set per worker, and every CLAUDE* and ANTHROPIC_* variable of this session is dropped
before the worker starts, so this session's routing and effort do not reach it.

The environment below lives for this one process only. Never export it in a profile:
it would route every Claude Code session on this machine through OpenRouter.
```

## Lessons it cites
